title: The residue test on the pro-étale site
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an integer
$n\geq1$ and $A=A_{E,n}$, put $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$, let $T$ be a
scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let
$K\in D^b_c(T_{\Proet},A)$ be a bounded constructible complex of
$A$-modules on the small pro-étale site in the intrinsic sense of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. For integers $a\leq b$, use Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] and derived tensor as in [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Then $K$ has finite
Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ if and
only if the derived tensor product $K\otimes_A^L\kappa_T$ with the
constant sheaf $\kappa_T$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$.

proof.text: Substitute the constant residue module in degree zero in the definition of Tor amplitude. This proves the forward implication for the chosen K-flat resolution.

Choose the recorded K-flat resolution Q -> K with flat terms. Prove invariance of tensor homology under a derived isomorphism between K-flat complexes: resolve the other tensor factor, use mapping cones and K-flatness to preserve quasi-isomorphisms in either variable, and descend homology of tensor with that resolution through localization at quasi-isomorphisms. The total-tensor/single-complex isomorphism identifies tensor with a module in degree zero with ordinary termwise tensor. Apply this comparison to P and Q to transfer the residue vanishing hypothesis to Q.

source.place: Tags 06YN and 06YS; explicit mapping-cone and localization argument

proof.text: The image r of the uniformizer has r^n=0 in A. Its principal ideal is maximal because the uniformizer generates the maximal ideal of the coefficient DVR and n>=1. For every module sheaf annihilated by r, apply the one-degree ordinary tensor calculation [lem-sf-proetale-residue-module-tensor-homology] to Q and the transferred residue vanishing.

For a natural scalar endomorphism eta and an extension-closed property W containing zero and all eta-killed objects, prove by induction that eta^n X=0 implies W(X). In the induction take I=image(eta_X): eta^(n-1) kills I, while eta kills coker(I -> X), by naturality and the image/cokernel identities. Apply this to W(M)=vanishing of degree-i homology of termwise Q tensor M. Each term of Q is flat, so a short exact sequence of modules gives a degreewise short exact sequence of tensor complexes; the exact homology segment makes W extension-closed. Hence Q tensor M vanishes for every M outside the interval. Compare Q with each K-flat resolution of each representative of K using the comparison in step 2. This supplies every quantifier in the unchanged definition of Tor amplitude.

proof_origin.place: G3 stage-3 proof: K-flat comparison, one-degree field-module calculation, and categorical nilpotent image/cokernel induction
